# superset_sql_query (Data Source)

Runs a SQL query through SQL Lab on a database connection and returns its rows, for example to create a dataset, a role or a user per row of a table. The query runs on every plan and refresh, so keep it cheap. The connection must be exposed in SQL Lab (`expose_in_sqllab`), a query that changes data needs DML allowed on it (`allow_dml`), and the user of the provider needs access to the database in SQL Lab.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# One row per region of the sales table, read through SQL Lab.
data "superset_sql_query" "regions" {
  database_name = "Warehouse"
  schema        = "public"
  sql           = "SELECT DISTINCT region FROM sales ORDER BY region"
}

# A row level security filter per region: the rows come back as maps of texts.
resource "superset_row_level_security" "region" {
  for_each = toset([for row in data.superset_sql_query.regions.rows : row.region])

  name   = "sales ${each.key}"
  tables = [superset_dataset.sales.id]
  clause = "region = '${each.key}'"
}

# Typed values, when the texts are not enough.
output "regions" {
  value = jsondecode(data.superset_sql_query.regions.rows_json)
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `sql` (String) The query. Superset appends its own `LIMIT`; with several statements only the result of the last one is returned.

### Optional

- `catalog` (String) Catalog (database, project or similar depending on the engine) to run in, on Superset 6 connections with several catalogs. Left to the default of the connection when unset.
- `database_id` (Number) Numeric identifier of the connection, looked up from `database_name` when that is set.
- `database_name` (String) Name of the database connection to run the query on. Exactly one of `database_name` and `database_id` must be set.
- `limit` (Number) Maximum number of rows returned. Defaults to 1000; Superset caps it at its `SQL_MAX_ROW`.
- `schema` (String) Schema the unqualified table names of the query are resolved in.
- `template_params` (String) JSON object with the values of the Jinja parameters of the query, for example `jsonencode({ region = "north" })` for `{{ region }}`; needs the `ENABLE_TEMPLATE_PROCESSING` feature flag.

### Read-Only

- `columns` (Attributes List) Columns of the result, in the order of the query. Superset 3.1 returns none for a query without rows. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--columns))
- `limited` (Boolean) Whether the rows were cut by `limit` or by the cap of Superset.
- `row_count` (Number) Number of rows returned.
- `rows` (List of Map of String) Rows of the result, each a map from the column name to the value as text: numbers and booleans as Superset wrote them, dates in ISO 8601, and null values left out of the map.
- `rows_json` (String) The rows as Superset serialised them, a JSON array of objects, for `jsondecode` when the types of the values matter.

<a id="nestedatt--columns"></a>
### Nested Schema for `columns`

Read-Only:

- `is_datetime` (Boolean) Whether the column holds dates or timestamps.
- `name` (String) Name of the column; duplicate names get a `__1`, `__2` suffix.
- `type` (String) Generic type of the column as Superset names it, for example `INTEGER` or `STRING`.
